title: Gifts to Future You: Setting and Holding Boundaries with Yourself
coreMove: A self-boundary is a kind rule for Future You: name the cue and one handle, then use a planned repair step when the old setup fails under pressure.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who overfill their own schedules
exampleSpecs.stakes: A calendar rule protects energy before the request arrives.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Before any action, Gwen allocates scarce evening energy between plans and volunteer work.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers caught between duty and capacity
exampleSpecs.stakes: A calendar rule needs follow-through when a live request presses on energy.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Oliver faces two bad options around staying longer or honoring the prior energy limit.

exampleSpecs.domain: school admin and student phone habits
exampleSpecs.audience: readers who rely on resolve against technology
exampleSpecs.stakes: Technology limits need friction in the setting, not just a harsher inner voice.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Maxime and Brielle let the lesson emerge through a short exchange about charging location and app access.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who need a personal drinking rule without shame
exampleSpecs.stakes: A food or alcohol rule needs a cue and follow-through before the social moment arrives.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Set up the expectation that Russell will fold, then reveal the planned follow-through.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who answer requests while rushed
exampleSpecs.stakes: A compressed exchange can show how a pre-made capacity rule speaks in the moment.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A short message exchange at the ferry booth lands the lesson between the lines.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who confuse a miss with a moral verdict
exampleSpecs.stakes: Food boundaries work better when the cue becomes repair information instead of shame.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Wade interrupts a routine and deliberately restarts it with a planned food choice.
